A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
re-irradiating patients with isolated neck recurrences following radical treatment is feasible with acceptable morbidity.
the management of isolated cervical recurrence is a challenging problem and requires a multidisciplinary approach.
re-irradiating patients with isolated neck recurrences is safe and effective, provided the dose is fractionated and given with a conventional fractionation regimen.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the current practice of salvage neck dissection for resectable neck recurrence and adjuvant reirradiation for post-operative neck recurrence following salvage surgery needs to be validated by high-quality prospective trials.
re-irradiated patients should be managed in a multi-disciplinary setting and should be offered treatment options based on their individual characteristics.
re-irradiating a previously irradiated neck should be considered as an option in selected patients with recurrent neck disease.
